concerns.text: Tasks T042-T048 (Reviewer Resolutions) implement metrics (Novelty Score, Truthfulness Penalty, 'Good vs. Shadow', 'Stupid Mirror' baseline, Irreducibility Test) that have NO corresponding Functional Requirement (FR) or Success Criterion (SC) in spec.md. The spec explicitly limits scope to self-consistency, calibration, and error detection (FR-001 to FR-007). These tasks constitute unapproved scope creep, violating the requirement that every task must map to a spec element.

Task T012 implements a 'confidence-prediction loss' using an internal proxy (majority vote). However, the plan.md explicitly mandates 'Teacher-Student Distillation' and 'Pre-computed Teacher Labels' (Complexity Tracking) as the required approach to 'break the tautological loop'. The task implements the spec's assumption but contradicts the plan's architectural decision. Since the plan is the implementation blueprint, this task cannot be executed as written without first resolving the plan/spec contradiction regarding the training objective.

Tasks T042-T048 reference philosophical reviewers (Ada Lovelace, Alan Turing, etc.) and specific qualitative verdicts ('Mirror, not Mind', 'Computationally Irreducible') that do not exist as IDs or defined entities in the spec.md or plan.md. These are stale tags from an external discussion not formalized in the current specification artifacts.

Task T046 requires implementing a 'Stupid Mirror' baseline (random confidence scores). The spec.md (US-02) only defines a 'shuffled-attention control' to isolate temporal recursion. There is no FR or SC requiring a random-confidence baseline. This task has no matching spec element.
